key_insight: EHR representations entangle patient physiology with care processes, and neither a single dataset nor cross-site outcome invariance alone can identify their separate contributions.
clinical_relevance: Differences in EHR-based predictions across hospitals may reflect testing practices and patient mix rather than changes in underlying biology.
method: Formalized latent physiology, test ordering, recorded laboratory values, representations, and clinical environments.
Used information-theoretic analysis and observationally equivalent models to establish identification limits.
Derived conditions under which universally measured tests or independent-error tests restore identification.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical results and a worked example showing a 9.6-percentage-point cross-site gap despite unchanged biology, rather than clinical validation.
watch_item: Report cross-site invariance analyses as tests of a joint hypothesis about biology, exclusion, and representation sufficiency—not as proof of biological invariance.
paper_title: The Dark Matter of Clinical Data: An Identification Limit on Disentangling Physiology from Care Process in electronic health records
